title: What is Minimum Wage Australia? Hourly to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Find out what is minimum wage Australia for 2026-27, how casual loading and super affect your pay, and how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the 38-hour week.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $52,257 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay. This assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave, overtime, or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for the lack of paid leave entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. If you use our timesheet, tick the casual loading checkbox and enter your base rate – do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it paid on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary or wages. It is not deducted from your pay. For 2026-27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. Super is calculated on your ordinary time earnings, including casual loading if applicable.

bodyMarkdown:
## What is Minimum Wage Australia? Understanding the Basics

If you have ever asked yourself **what is minimum wage australia**, you are not alone. The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum pay that most employees in Australia must receive. From 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission set it at **$26.44 per hour** for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week. That works out to **$1,004.90 per week** and **$52,257 per year** before tax and super.

But the National Minimum Wage is just one piece of the puzzle. Many workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum rate. The figures here are the legal floor – your actual pay may be higher depending on your industry, role, and experience.

### How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual salary**

We assume a full-time week of **38 hours** (the standard under the Fair Work Act). If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the hours per week accordingly. For example:

- $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year
- $45 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $88,920 per year

This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a simple estimate, not a binding determination of your pay.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Reference

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay. For the National Minimum Wage:

- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

This can help you compare offers or budget between pay cycles.

## Casual Loading: Extra Pay for Flexibility

Casual employees receive a **25% loading** on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is therefore **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 + 25%).

If you are a casual worker, use our [timesheet](/) to calculate your pay. Enter your **base hourly rate** (the rate before loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading – the tool will add it for you.

Award rates for casuals also include the 25% loading unless the award specifies a different arrangement. Always check your award or agreement for the correct rate.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Earnings

Superannuation guarantee is **12% of your ordinary earnings** for 2026-27. Your employer must pay this on top of your salary or wages – it is not deducted from your pay. The super is calculated on your ordinary time earnings, which includes casual loading if you are a casual employee.

There is a maximum contribution base of **$270,830 per year**. If your ordinary earnings exceed this amount, your employer only needs to pay super on the first $270,830.

For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $52,257 per year:
- Super contribution: 12% × $52,257 = $6,270.84
- Total cost to employer: $52,257 + $6,270.84 = $58,527.84

Super is a valuable part of your total remuneration package. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax on Your Salary: 2026-27 Resident Rates

Income tax is deducted from your pay by your employer using the Pay As You Go (PAYG) system. The 2026-27 tax rates for Australian residents are:

- **Nil** on the first $18,200
- **15%** on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- **30%** on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- **37%** on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- **45%** on income above $190,000

Most people also pay the **Medicare levy of 2%** (the single reduction thresholds used here are from 2025-26 as the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed). The levy is applied to your taxable income after the tax-free threshold.

Tax estimates on this site do not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

## Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most industries have specific **award rates** that are higher. For example, the Hospitality Industry General Award or the Manufacturing Award set minimum rates for those sectors.

If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay is the award rate, not the National Minimum Wage. Always check your award or enterprise agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award.

### Average Earnings for Comparison

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports **Average Weekly Earnings (AWE)** for full-time adult employees. As of May 2026, the average full-time ordinary time earnings were **$2,083.70 per week** (or about $108,352 per year). This is an average across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job. Your actual pay may differ significantly.

For all employees (including part-time), the average total earnings were **$1,579.20 per week**. These figures help you see where the National Minimum Wage sits relative to the broader workforce.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more tools and information, visit our [reference tables](/data) or read about [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).
